literal: family. This is not an idiom, just the literal word.
usage: "3eila" is the standard word for family in Egyptian Arabic, often referring to the extended family or the family unit as a whole. When Cairenes talk about their immediate family or parents living in the same house, they frequently use "ahl" (folks). Both are used in casual and formal everyday speech.

variants.label: my family
variants.note: The most common way to refer to your own family.

variants.label: your family (to a man)
variants.note: Used when asking a male about his family.

variants.label: your family (to a woman)
variants.note: Used when asking a female about her family.

variants.label: my folks / immediate family
variants.note: Used specifically to refer to parents or immediate family members.

responses.english: May God keep them for you.

examples.english: How is your family? (to a man)

examples.transliteration: ana hat3ashsha ma3a ahli el naharda.
examples.english: I will have dinner with my folks today.
